title: PEOPLE & TREASURES
blurb: A child, a head, an ear, and the two things once held most precious.

radicals.name: CHILD
radicals.origin: A baby wrapped in a blanket: a big head, and two arms held out to be picked up.
ex: the small 小 child of your child
a child under a roof, being taught
a child 子 under a roof 宀: characters were said to multiply like children
radicals.watch: 子 is also a common ending for nouns, with no child in it: 桌子 (table), 杯子 (cup). And 好 (good), a woman with her child, is filed under woman.

radicals.name: HEAD
radicals.origin: A kneeling person with an enormous head. As a word 页 now means a page, but as a radical it still means the head.
radicals.clue: the head, the face and the neck
ex: to look back, to look after
radicals.watch: The head comes first, so the hint stretches to what comes first: 题 (title, topic), 预 (in advance), 顺 (in order). Look-alike: 贝 (money) is the same shape without the two strokes on top.

radicals.name: EAR
radicals.origin: An ear, drawn with its folds. The everyday word is 耳朵.
ex: quick ears: 聪明 is sharp of hearing and of mind
the feeling that makes your ears burn
radicals.watch: The commonest hearing words moved away: 听 (to listen) is written with a mouth, and 闻 (to hear, to smell) keeps its ear inside a door. The two radicals nicknamed ears, ⻖ and ⻏, have nothing to do with hearing.

radicals.name: SPIRIT
radicals.origin: 示 is an altar: a stone table with an offering on it. On the left of a character it slims down to 礻.
ex: the character pasted on doors at New Year
the full 示 sits at the bottom
radicals.watch: One dot apart: 礻 (spirit) has one dot on its right side, 衤 (clothes) has two. 社 (society) began as the shrine of the village god, and 礼 (manners, a gift) as a ceremony.

radicals.name: JADE
radicals.origin: 玉 is jade: three discs on a string. As a radical it loses its dot and looks exactly like 王, a king, with the bottom stroke tilted up.
ex: at first a ring of jade
at first a round jade bead
radicals.watch: It is named after the king, but it nearly always means jade. The hint has worn away in some very common members: 现 (now), 玩 (to play), 班 (class). 理 (reason) once meant cutting jade along its grain.
